BY ADV Dinesh Mathew J Murikan  THIS MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS APPEAL HAVING BEEN FINALLY HEARD ON 11.12.2024, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 MACA.360/2014  3  2024:KER:94150  JUDGMENT Dated this the 11th day of December, 2024
Appellant is the son of the petitioner in OP(MV).No.1186/2007 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Irinjalakuda.
He filed the above claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation on account of the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 11.6.2006.

According to the petitioner, while he was walking through NH 47 from Meloor to Kadukutty Junction, a lorry bearing Registration No.TN-37-Z-1029, driven by the 2nd respondent in a rash and negligent manner in high speed, hit him down resulting in causing head injury.
2. 1st respondent is the owner, 2nd respondent is the driver and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the said lorry.
According to the appellant, after the incident, the petitioner was bed ridden till he breath his last on 2.11.2019.
In the circumstances, with the leave of the court, this appeal was filed by his son.
During the pendency of the appeal, the petitioner died and additional appellants 2 to 5 were impleaded as his legal 2024:KER:94150 representatives.
They are his wife and children.
Additional 2 nd appellant is his widow and additional appellants 3 to 5 are his children.
3. In the incident, he sustained lacerated wound on the scalp, 8x1x0.5 cm as seen from Exhibit A2 wound certificate.
Exhibit A3 is the treatment cum discharge certificate issued from St.James Hospital, Chalakudy, which shows that he was admitted in the hospital from 11.3.2006 to 1.5.2006,
Exhibit A10 is case sheet issued from St. James Hospital which shows that he had suffered with severe head injury affecting the neurological system damaging the mobility and other faculties.
Exhibist A5 and A6 discharge summaries show that he was admitted in the hospital from 19.7.2006 to 20.7.2006 and from 29.7.2006 to 4.8.2006 respectively.
4. PW4, the doctor who treated him deposed that the petitioner has aphasia, with poorly tested attention, no concentration, registration or other cognitive functions.
His speech and memory are grossly impaired.
Cranial nerve palsies of 9,10,11 and 12 cranial nerves.

He is totally bedridden,
cannot stand without support.
He cannot walk or use his lower limbs for any purposeful locomotion.

sentences.text:
Similarly his upper limb 2024:KER:94150 also cannot be used for the day to day life for having food,
bathing, dressing and cleaning himself.
He has gross ataxia, poor finger hand co- ordination.
Recurrent episodes of epilepsy controlled with medication and needs to continue the anti epileptic medicines life long.
His total permanent disability is thus assessed as 100%.
5. The evidence in the case consists of the oral testimonies of PWs1 to 4 and documents Exhibits A1 to A10.
No evidence was adduced by the respondents.
Exhibit X1 Medical report was also marked.
After evaluating the available evidence, the Tribunal awarded a total sum of Rs.7,37,630/- along with interest @ 7.5% per annum from 26.10.2007 till deposition.
Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded, the petitioner preferred this appeal.

6. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the amount of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?

7. Heard Sri. T.N. Manoj, the learned counsel for the appellant and Sri. Dinesh Mathew J Muricken,
the learned counsel for the 3 rd respondent.
2024:
8 . The point: The fact that 1st respondent is the owner of the lorry, 2nd respondent is the driver and 3rd respondent is the insurer, is not in dispute.

From Exhibit A1 FIR and Exhibit A4 charge sheet,
the negligence of the 2nd respondent stands proved.

The 3rd respondent has no case that there is any violation of the policy conditions and as such 3 rd respondent is liable to indemnify the liability of the 1 st respondent in respect of the above vehicle.
9. Petitioner claimed that his monthly income is Rs.5,000/- and the Tribunal reduced the same to Rs.3500/-.
In the light of the decision in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance [(2011) 13 SCC 236] the notional income of the petitioner is liable to be fixed at Rs.5500/-.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance [(2011) 13 SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the fact that the petitioner was aged 44 years at the time of the accident, the multiplier to be applied is 14.
He is also entitled to enhancement in monthly income on account of future prospects at the rate of 25%, in the light of the decision in National Insurance Co.Ltd v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680].

entities.text: National Insurance Co.Ltd v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, his monthly income is to be considered as Rs.6875/-.
The fact that the petitioner sustained 100% disability is not disputed.

In the above 2024:KER:94150 circumstances, loss on account of permanent disability will come to Rs.11,55,000/-
(6875x12x14).The
tribunal
has awarded only Rs.6,30,000/- on that account.
Therefore, the compensation towards loss of permanent disability is to be modified accordingly.

10. It has come out in evidence that the petitioner sustained injuries on 11.3.2006 and thereafter he was bedridden till he breathed his last on 2.11.2019 ie., he was bedridden for a period of more than 13 years and 7 months.
The Tribunal has awarded only Rs.500/- towards extra nourishment.

Considering the fact that the petitioner was bedridden for such a long period, the compensation in that respect is enhanced to Rs.1,00,000/-
Vidyanandan vs M.Ponnuswami on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184987400/
3 11.

entities.text: Vidyanandan vs M.Ponnuswami on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Towards bystander expenses, the tribunal has awarded only a meager sum of Rs.9,300/-.
Similarly, towards pain and suffering, only a sum of Rs.20,000/- was awarded.

In the above circumstances, considering the fact that the petitioner was bedridden for a period of more than 13 years and 7 months, I hold that towards pain and suffering, and bystander expenses together, a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- each can be awarded.
Towards loss of amenities, the tribunal has awarded only Rs.10,000/- though there was a claim for Rs.1,00,000.
Considering the facts, compensation towards loss of amenities is enhanced to Rs.1,00,000/-.
13. Though the petitioner claimed a sum of Rs. 60,000 towards loss of earnings, no amount seen awarded without assigning any reasons.
In the above circumstances, since the petitioner was bed ridden for a long period after the incident, Rs.60,000/- can be awarded in that head.
No change is required on other heads, as compensation awarded on those heads appears reasonable.

Therefore,
the total compensation due to the appellant will come to Rs.17,92,130/-, as detailed in the table given below:
